steps.name: Import counts, QC, and fit DESeq2 three-group model
caveats: Salmon counts are estimates and may be non-integer; round rather than truncate, and report the magnitude of the change
With n=4 per group a single aberrant replicate can dominate a PCA axis — inspect the sample-distance heatmap before concluding a group is heterogeneous
12,000 genes is smaller than a typical full annotation, suggesting pre-filtering upstream; report this rather than assuming transcriptome-wide coverage
steps.context: Human liver bulk RNA-seq, single batch, unpaired, 3 groups x 4 replicates. No covariates other than condition are present in the metadata, so the design is ~condition and nothing else can be adjusted for. Gene identifiers are HGNC-style symbols, which is what downstream gene-set files use.
steps.question: Do the 12 liver samples cluster by condition (control, treated_a, treated_b), are all 4 replicates per group usable, and does a single DESeq2 ~condition model fit cleanly over the 12,000-gene Salmon count matrix?
constraints: Fit DESeq() exactly once on all 12 samples; do not subset to pairs of groups and refit
Set control as the factor reference level explicitly with relevel(); do not rely on alphabetical ordering
Do not drop any sample on QC grounds without stating the quantitative reason and reporting results both with and without it
Do not perform any batch correction — the design is single-batch and no batch variable exists
steps.description: Load /eval-full-32-without-multi-group-3x4-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 sample columns, first column gene symbol) and /eval-full-32-without-multi-group-3x4-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows, sample id + condition). Verify the sample columns of the count matrix and the metadata rows match exactly as sets and reorder metadata to the count column order; abort with a clear message if they do not. Collapse duplicate gene symbols if any exist, by summing counts, and report how many. Set condition as a factor with control as the explicit reference level. Number of genes retained after the >=10 counts in >=4 samples filter is reported, out of the 12,000 input genes
condition factor reference level is explicitly control, and this is stated in the output

PCA on VST data and a sample-distance heatmap are produced, with percent variance for PC1/PC2 and an explicit written statement of whether condition separates the samples and whether any replicate is a potential outlier
Fitted DESeqDataSet, VST matrix and normalized counts are saved to disk for downstream steps

steps.name: Omnibus LRT across the three groups
caveats: With 4 replicates per group the LRT may return few or zero genes at padj < 0.05; if so, report the number at padj < 0.10 and the top-ranked genes by statistic, and state explicitly that absence of significant hits at n=4 is weak evidence of no effect rather than evidence of no effect
A non-uniform p-value histogram (e.g. bimodal or U-shaped) indicates a model or dispersion problem and must be reported, not smoothed over
steps.context: n=4 per group; the LRT with 2 numerator degrees of freedom is the appropriate omnibus test for a 3-level factor with count data, and DESeq2's shrunken dispersions are what make it usable at this sample size.
steps.question: Which genes differ across control, treated_a and treated_b at all — i.e. which genes show any condition effect under a likelihood-ratio test of ~condition versus ~1?
constraints: Use DESeq(..., test='LRT', reduced=~1) on the object from T1S1; do not approximate the omnibus test with an ANOVA on normalized counts or with a union of pairwise hits
Report BH-adjusted p-values; do not report raw p-value counts as the headline result
Do not interpret the log2FoldChange column emitted alongside an LRT as the effect size for the omnibus test — replace or clearly relabel it
steps.description: Using the DESeqDataSet fitted in T1S1, run the DESeq2 likelihood-ratio test with full design ~condition and reduced design ~1. This is the direct answer to the 'differ across the three groups at all' half of the question: it tests the joint null that all three group means are equal, without picking a direction. Extract the full results table (LRT statistic, p-value, BH-adjusted p-value, and the baseMean), and report the number of genes at padj < 0.05 and at padj < 0.10. Because an LRT log2FoldChange is only the coefficient for one arbitrary level and is not the effect size being tested, replace it in the reported table with the per-group mean of VST expression and the maximum absolute pairwise difference between group means, so each significant gene carries an interpretable effect magnitude. Produce a p-value histogram to check the null behaviour of the test, and a heatmap of VST values (row-scaled) for the top 50 LRT genes with samples annotated by condition. Save the complete ranked LRT table to disk.
acceptance_criteria: LRT results table for all filtered genes is saved, with LRT statistic, raw p, BH padj, baseMean, per-group VST means and max pairwise group-mean difference
Counts of genes at padj < 0.05 and padj < 0.10 are reported explicitly
A p-value histogram is produced and its shape is commented on (uniform-with-spike versus anomalous)
Row-scaled VST heatmap of the top 50 LRT genes with condition annotation is produced
The report states plainly that the LRT identifies that a difference exists somewhere among the three groups and does not say which groups differ

steps.name: Pairwise Wald contrasts: treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control
caveats: n=4 per group gives good power only for large, consistent effects; report median absolute log2FC among significant genes so the reader can judge whether hits are of plausible magnitude or driven by low-count noise
Genes with very low baseMean can produce extreme fold changes; rely on the shrunken LFC for ranking and flag any top hit whose baseMean is in the bottom decile
DESeq2's independent filtering sets padj to NA for low-count genes — report how many genes were filtered this way per contrast rather than treating NA as non-significant
steps.context: control is the reference level set in T1S1, so both contrasts are oriented as treatment-minus-control: positive log2FC means higher in the treatment. Both contrasts come from the same fitted model, so they share dispersion estimates and the size factors computed over all 12 samples.
steps.question: Which genes does treated_a change relative to control, and which genes does treated_b change relative to control, with direction and effect size?
constraints: Use the single DESeqDataSet from T1S1 with Wald tests via results(contrast=...); do not refit separate two-group models per contrast
Apply BH correction separately within each contrast; do not pool the two contrasts into one multiple-testing family, and do not restrict the tested gene set to the T1S2 LRT hits
Use apeglm shrinkage for ranking and plots only; report unshrunk log2FC and p-values in the results tables
State the direction convention (positive = up in treatment relative to control) explicitly in the output
steps.description: From the T1S1 fit, run Wald tests for the two contrasts of interest: treated_a vs control and treated_b vs control. Each contrast gets its own results() call with independent BH multiple-testing correction across the filtered gene set — the two treatments are separate questions and must not be pooled into one FDR family, and the gene set tested must be the full filtered set, not the LRT-significant subset. For each contrast report: number of genes at padj < 0.05 with |log2FC| > 1 and at padj < 0.05 with no fold-change cut, split by direction (up/down). Compute apeglm-shrunken LFCs for stable ranking and visualisation while keeping the unshrunk log2FC, lfcSE, stat and p-value in the saved table. Produce per-contrast MA plots and volcano plots (labelled with the top genes by padj), and save both full ranked results tables plus a ranking statistic column suitable for GSEA input (recommended: sign(log2FC) * -log10(pvalue), or the Wald stat) for use by T2S1.
acceptance_criteria: Two complete results tables are saved, one per contrast, each with unshrunk log2FC, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj, baseMean, and an apeglm-shrunken log2FC column
Each contrast's BH correction is applied independently over the full filtered gene set; this is stated in the output
DE gene counts are reported per contrast, split by direction, at padj<0.05 and at padj<0.05 with |log2FC|>1
MA plot and volcano plot are produced for each contrast
A ranking statistic column is present in both saved tables for downstream GSEA

steps.name: Reconcile omnibus and pairwise results; compare the two treatments
caveats: The significant-in-one-but-not-the-other pattern is the classic difference-of-significance fallacy; the direct treated_b vs treated_a contrast is the only evidence that bears on differential response and it is the least powered of the three
Discordant-direction genes at n=4 are frequently noise; require a meaningful |log2FC| in both contrasts before highlighting one
steps.context: This step answers the implicit comparative question: three groups with a shared control invite the question of whether the two treatments do the same thing. The classification is descriptive labelling built from three independently corrected tests, not a formal interaction test.
steps.question: Of the genes the LRT flags as differing across the three groups, which are driven by treated_a alone, by treated_b alone, or shared by both — and which genes differ between treated_a and treated_b directly?
constraints: Derive the treated_b vs treated_a contrast from the same T1S1 fitted object; do not refit
Classify using padj thresholds consistently and state the threshold used
Do not claim a gene responds differently to the two treatments on the basis of one contrast being significant and the other not — point to the treated_b vs treated_a contrast for that claim
steps.description: Integrate the T1S2 LRT table and the two T1S3 contrast tables into one gene-level summary. Add the third pairwise Wald contrast, treated_b vs treated_a (from the same T1S1 fit, independently BH-corrected), so the two treatments can be compared to each other and not only to control. Build a joined table keyed on gene symbol carrying: LRT padj, and for each of the three contrasts the log2FC and padj. Classify each LRT-significant gene into treated_a-specific, treated_b-specific, shared-concordant (same direction in both treatments), or shared-discordant (opposite directions), using padj<0.05 in the relevant contrasts, and report the counts in each class. Produce a Venn or UpSet diagram of the DE gene sets from the three contrasts, and a scatter plot of treated_a-vs-control log2FC against treated_b-vs-control log2FC over all tested genes, with the Pearson and Spearman correlation and the identity line drawn, which shows at a glance whether the two treatments act along the same axis or divergently. Save the joined table.
acceptance_criteria: A joined per-gene table is saved containing LRT padj plus log2FC and padj for all three pairwise contrasts (treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control, treated_b vs treated_a)
Counts of treated_a-specific, treated_b-specific, shared-concordant and shared-discordant genes among LRT-significant genes are reported
An UpSet or Venn diagram of the three contrasts' DE gene sets is produced
A log2FC-vs-log2FC scatter of the two treatment-vs-control contrasts is produced with Pearson and Spearman correlation reported
The output states that 'treatment-specific' here means significant in one contrast and not the other, which is not the same as a significant difference between the two effects

steps.name: Gene-set enrichment for each treatment contrast
caveats: If neither human hallmark nor human GO-BP sets can be resolved at run time, report the absence explicitly and deliver the ranked gene lists alone — the per-gene results from T1S2/T1S3 remain the primary answer and the run should not be treated as failed

GSEA can return significant sets even when no individual gene passes FDR; that is a legitimate gain in power but it must be reported as a coordinated-shift signal, not as evidence that individual leading-edge genes are differentially expressed
GO BP sets are heavily nested, so significant hits will arrive in correlated blocks
steps.context: The background for enrichment must be the genes actually tested in T1S3 after filtering, not all 12,000 input genes and not a genome-wide universe; the counts matrix appears already pre-filtered, which restricts the achievable universe and should be stated.
steps.question: Which hallmark and GO biological-process gene sets are coordinately shifted by treated_a versus control and by treated_b versus control in liver, and do the two treatments engage the same programmes?
constraints: Use the ranking statistic column from T1S3, not a thresholded DE gene list, and do not re-derive rankings from raw counts
Use human gene sets only — the environment also holds mouse and rat pathway files and selecting one of those would produce confident nonsense on human data
Report BH-adjusted p-values and set sizes alongside NES; never report a pathway hit without its set size and leading-edge count
Collapse or flag redundant parent/child GO terms before reporting a headline count of enriched processes
steps.description: Run rank-based gene set enrichment (fgsea) separately on the two ranked gene lists produced in T1S3 — treated_a vs control and treated_b vs control — using the full ranked list of tested genes rather than a thresholded subset, so the analysis does not inherit the low power of the per-gene cutoff. Required reference data: human hallmark gene sets and human GO biological-process gene sets, both keyed on HGNC gene symbols, which is the identifier space of the counts matrix (a human hallmark GMT and a human GO-BP GMT are present in the environment's pathway reference collection; resolve them at run time rather than assuming a path). Restrict sets to those with between 15 and 500 genes present in the tested background. Report the top enriched sets per contrast by adjusted p-value with NES and leading-edge genes, and produce a side-by-side comparison of NES for sets significant in either contrast so shared versus treatment-specific programmes are visible. Since the tissue is liver, explicitly note whether hepatocyte-relevant programmes (xenobiotic and drug metabolism, bile acid metabolism, fatty acid metabolism, inflammatory response) appear, as these are the expected axes for a liver treatment response — report their absence just as plainly as their presence.
acceptance_criteria: fgsea results tables for both contrasts are saved with pathway, NES, p-value, BH padj, set size and leading-edge genes
The gene-set collections actually used are named in the output, with their organism (human) confirmed to match the data
The ranked list used is the full tested gene set from T1S3, and the number of ranked genes and the number of sets tested after the 15-500 size filter are reported
A comparison of NES between the two contrasts for sets significant in either is produced
Liver-relevant programmes are explicitly commented on, present or absent

plan.title: Liver RNA-seq: omnibus LRT + treated_a/treated_b vs control
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single-batch bulk RNA-seq experiment in human liver: raw Salmon gene-level counts (12,000 genes x 12 samples, gene symbols in column 1) with a 12-row metadata table carrying one `condition` column with three levels — control, treated_a, treated_b — 4 unpaired replicates each. The research question has two distinct parts, and they need two distinct statistics, so the plan keeps them separate rather than collapsing one into the other.

Part 1 ('which genes differ across the three groups at all') is an omnibus question: it is answered by a DESeq2 likelihood-ratio test of ~condition against the intercept-only reduced model ~1, which asks whether any group differs without committing to a direction. Part 2 ('which genes does each treatment change relative to control') is two pairwise Wald contrasts, treated_a vs control and treated_b vs control, each with its own independent BH correction — the two contrasts are separate scientific questions and must not share a single FDR family, nor be filtered through the LRT gene set (that would be a two-stage procedure with an uncontrolled error rate). T1S1 fits one DESeq2 object over all 12 samples so that dispersion is estimated from the full design (12 samples, 3 groups) rather than from 8-sample subsets, and emits QC (library sizes, VST PCA, sample-sample correlation) that establishes whether the group structure is the dominant variance axis and whether any replicate is an outlier — 4 per group leaves no room to lose one silently.

T1S2 then reads the same fitted object for the omnibus LRT; T1S3 for the two Wald contrasts with LFC shrinkage (apeglm) for ranking, keeping unshrunk log2FC and p-values for reporting. T1S4 is the integrative step the question implicitly asks for: which LRT genes are driven by treated_a alone, by treated_b alone, or shared, plus the direct treated_a vs treated_b contrast, so the two treatments can be compared to one another rather than only to control. T2S1 puts the ranked contrast statistics through gene-set enrichment against staged human hallmark and GO-BP sets (confirmed present under /mnt/refs, HGNC symbols — matching the counts matrix's gene-symbol index, so no ID mapping is needed).

Power is the honest limitation throughout: n=4 per group is adequate for large, consistent effects and underpowered for modest ones, so the plan requires effect-size reporting alongside FDR and forbids presenting an empty or tiny result set as evidence of no effect.

steps.name: Gene-set enrichment for each treatment contrast
steps.question: Which hallmark and GO biological-process gene sets are coordinately shifted by treated_a versus control and by treated_b versus control in liver, and do the two treatments engage the same programmes?
steps.description: Run rank-based gene set enrichment (fgsea) separately on the two ranked gene lists produced in T1S3 — treated_a vs control and treated_b vs control — using the full ranked list of tested genes rather than a thresholded subset, so the analysis does not inherit the low power of the per-gene cutoff. Required reference data: human hallmark gene sets and human GO biological-process gene sets, both keyed on HGNC gene symbols, which is the identifier space of the counts matrix (a human hallmark GMT and a human GO-BP GMT are present in the environment's pathway reference collection; resolve them at run time rather than assuming a path). Restrict sets to those with between 15 and 500 genes present in the tested background. Report the top enriched sets per contrast by adjusted p-value with NES and leading-edge genes, and produce a side-by-side comparison of NES for sets significant in either contrast so shared versus treatment-specific programmes are visible. Since the tissue is liver, explicitly note whether hepatocyte-relevant programmes (xenobiotic and drug metabolism, bile acid metabolism, fatty acid metabolism, inflammatory response) appear, as these are the expected axes for a liver treatment response — report their absence just as plainly as their presence.
steps.context: The background for enrichment must be the genes actually tested in T1S3 after filtering, not all 12,000 input genes and not a genome-wide universe; the counts matrix appears already pre-filtered, which restricts the achievable universe and should be stated.
acceptance_criteria: fgsea results tables for both contrasts are saved with pathway, NES, p-value, BH padj, set size and leading-edge genes
The gene-set collections actually used are named in the output, with their organism (human) confirmed to match the data
The ranked list used is the full tested gene set from T1S3, and the number of ranked genes and the number of sets tested after the 15-500 size filter are reported
A comparison of NES between the two contrasts for sets significant in either is produced
Liver-relevant programmes are explicitly commented on, present or absent
constraints: Use the ranking statistic column from T1S3, not a thresholded DE gene list, and do not re-derive rankings from raw counts
Use human gene sets only — the environment also holds mouse and rat pathway files and selecting one of those would produce confident nonsense on human data
Report BH-adjusted p-values and set sizes alongside NES; never report a pathway hit without its set size and leading-edge count
Collapse or flag redundant parent/child GO terms before reporting a headline count of enriched processes
caveats: If neither human hallmark nor human GO-BP sets can be resolved at run time, report the absence explicitly and deliver the ranked gene lists alone — the per-gene results from T1S2/T1S3 remain the primary answer and the run should not be treated as failed

GSEA can return significant sets even when no individual gene passes FDR; that is a legitimate gain in power but it must be reported as a coordinated-shift signal, not as evidence that individual leading-edge genes are differentially expressed
GO BP sets are heavily nested, so significant hits will arrive in correlated blocks
